review_scope: Independent sixth-round review of the round-6 Writer submission - a one-value schema recovery in which layouts/partials/schema-github-copilot-usage-metrics-guide-2026.html changed "@type": "TechArticle" to "Article" and nothing else. All five registered documentation pages were re-opened by the reviewer in this run (S1, S3, S4, S6, S7; HTTP 200 on 2026-11-19 between 16:04Z and 16:05Z) and every material numerical, endpoint, permission, field and definitional claim in the body was matched against the live text. sources.note: GitHub Copilot usage metrics REST reference. Supplies the report endpoint families, the signed-download-link response shape, the per-scope fine-grained permissions and PAT scopes, the October 10, 2025 availability date and the one-year retention limit. Re-fetched in this run (HTTP 200); the organization read:org sentence and the enterprise manage_billing:copilot/read:enterprise sentence were both read directly from the live page text.

GitHub Copilot usage metrics concept page. Supplies the five-category table, the 'Look for patterns across these signals...' sentence, the coverage statement, the two-full-UTC-day latency, the organization non-additivity rule, the activity-versus-license distinction and the repository-insights telemetry note. Re-fetched in this run (HTTP 200). This page contains no occurrence of '28' or '1 year', which is why those attributions were corrected.

Metrics and API/export field reference. Supplies the dashboard metric definitions used in the Adoption, Engagement and Acceptance Rate sections (DAU, WAU, average chat requests per active user, code completion acceptance rate), the active/passive code-review definitions, the per-user field list (user_id, user_login, ai_credits_used, used_* indicators, ai_adoption_phase) and the totals_by_ide / totals_by_feature / totals_by_language_feature arrays. Re-fetched in this run (HTTP 200); it contains no 'directional' wording.

Team-level Copilot usage metrics recipe. Supplies the two-report join, the user-teams key fields, the one-row-per-user-team-pair grain and the under-5-seated-user exclusion with its shortfall consequence. Re-fetched in this run (HTTP 200).

GitHub 'Reconciling Copilot usage metrics' guide. Supplies the organization-attribution model: 'Organization-level Copilot usage metrics are based on organization membership, not on where individual actions occur'; the requirement that a user have an active Copilot seat within the enterprise to appear in its metrics; the attribution of a seated user's usage to every organization in that enterprise they belong to regardless of where the seat is assigned; the dedicated-administrative-organization example; and 'Enterprise-level reports deduplicate users across organizations. Organization-level reports do not.' Re-fetched in this run (HTTP 200) and read directly from the page text.

claims.note: Headline and description name the metric categories and API reporting only; no measured value, ranking or vendor performance figure is asserted.

Opening framing: a hypothetical 200-person organization supplies the stakes, and the claim that GitHub exposes dashboards, REST APIs and NDJSON exports is linked to the concept page in the same paragraph. No organization was measured.
Two hypothetical adoption/engagement profiles explain why DAU alone does not show depth; the paragraph states the 80%, two and fifteen figures are illustrative, not measured benchmarks.

Judgement paragraph about acceptance rate as a target. The 40% and 80% rates are now explicitly labelled in the sentence as a hypothetical illustration, not measured acceptance rates; no tenant was queried and no acceptance figure is asserted.

Verbatim quote of the concept page's 'Look for patterns across these signals' advice (S3). The 50/5/200 line counts that follow are now labelled in place as an illustration, not a measured comparison; the sentence asserts no observed line counts.

Two-full-UTC-day latency is the concept page's sentence (S3); the *-28-day/latest report endpoints returning 'the previous 28 days' are documented in the REST reference (S1). The unsupported '28-day dashboard rolling window' claim was deleted in this round.

Scoped availability, re-checked against both sources on 2026-11-19T15:18Z. S1 states 'Reports are available starting from October 10, 2025, and historical data can be accessed for up to 1 year from the current date' only inside the enterprise report sections (enterprise-1-day and the enterprise users-1-day endpoint); none of the four organization endpoint sections carries an availability or retention sentence, which the article now says. S7 supplies the organization date verbatim: 'Organization-level reports are available starting December 12, 2025.' The paragraph keeps both dates as documented availability, not observed backfill, and states no measured date.
Endpoint paths verified on the REST reference (S1, HTTP 200 on 2026-11-19): enterprise-1-day, enterprise-28-day/latest, users-1-day, users-28-day/latest and the organization equivalents.

Opening lines of the daily pull sketch: variables, output directory and the two-step comment. Not executed against any organization; the article now calls it a sketch instead of a script you can run as-is, and the header comment says the same.

Step 1 of the sketch: one authenticated GET per report family per day, saving the JSON envelope. Endpoint paths and the envelope shape follow S1; the token placeholder stays redacted. Not run against a tenant.

Step 2 of the sketch: jq extracts the download_links array from the saved envelope and curl fetches the NDJSON behind each signed link, which is what S1's documented response ({'download_links': [...], 'report_day': ...}) requires. The loop was exercised once against a local fixture envelope in this run's scratch directory (file:// links, four stub NDJSON lines) to confirm the extraction and download path; no GitHub API call was made.
Closing line of the sketch, counting downloaded NDJSON lines. No count from any real report is presented anywhere in the article.

Report families, the per-user grain keyed by user_id and the user-teams key fields (user_id, user_login, day, organization_id/enterprise_id, team_id, slug) are quoted from the team-level page (S6) and corroborated by S4's user-teams table.
The two documented user-teams endpoint paths; S1 lists both enterprise and organization variants, S6 shows them in its fetching table.
Pandas sketch following the documented recipe: both inputs are same-day reports, join on user_id, group by team_id with slug for display. Not executed against a live tenant; the article says so.
The under-5-seated-user exclusion and the resulting shortfall in team sums are documented on the team-level metrics page (S6, HTTP 200 on 2026-11-19).
Definitional split between usage metrics and the user management API, quoted from the concept page (S3). No seat or usage count is compared in this article.

Restates the documented non-additivity rule (S3): organization totals overlap because one user can belong to several organizations. The deduplication half of the sentence, 'Users are deduplicated at the enterprise level', is documented on S7, which states that enterprise-level reports deduplicate users across organizations and organization-level reports do not. No count is compared.

Users identified only through server-side telemetry counting toward active users while missing from breakdown arrays is documented on S4 and S3. The advice to measure the gap locally is guidance, and the article states no share is published.
Qualitative argument that lines of code is directional at best. The 100 and 500 line counts are now labelled in place as a hypothetical illustration of the ranking problem, not measured output.
Pitfall restating the documented processing delay (S3); no real-time latency measurement is claimed.
Repository-level reports using server-side pull request and review data with no dependence on IDE telemetry is the concept page's own statement (S3).
Methodological guidance: cross-referencing adoption with DORA metrics is framed as a correlation hypothesis, not attribution. No measurement is claimed.

Closing restatement of the five documented categories, the activity-versus-seat distinction and the two-day processing delay (S3); the 'faster' outcome is framed as what the reporting can inform, not a measured result.
Internal links to two related posts on this site; no external factual claim.

Organization attribution paragraph, re-hashed against the current text. The membership rule, the enterprise seat requirement, attribution to every organization in the enterprise and the dedicated-administration-organization example are S7's own sentences (re-read 2026-11-19T15:18Z); the overlap/non-additivity sentence is S3's.

Bullet list re-hashed against the current text. Each bullet restates S7's organization-attribution description: seat inside the enterprise, usage in multiple organization dashboards, enterprise-level deduplication, and dedicated administrative organizations. No figure is attached to any bullet.

Implication paragraph re-hashed against the current text. Deduplication is S7's documented behaviour and non-additivity is S3's documented rule; the overstatement of a summed org DAU is stated qualitatively, with no computed or measured magnitude.

title_options: GitHub Copilot Usage Metrics: Categories and API Reporting
Which Copilot Usage Number Can You Defend? Report Categories and API Access
GitHub Copilot Metrics API: Report Shapes, Attribution Rules and Team Joins
presentation.title_rationale: The selected title names the product and the two things the article is organised around - the metric categories and the API that reports them - in 58 characters, so a reader scanning a results page knows what they get. The reader problem (which number survives a renewal review) is carried by the description and the introduction instead of being squeezed into the headline.
presentation.visual_purpose: The cover maps the documented report families to the team-totals join: aggregated enterprise/organization reports, the per-user report, and the user-teams report, with the join key and the under-5-seated-user exclusion that makes team sums fall short of entity totals. It is drawn from S1/S3/S4/S6 wording only; no tenant was queried and no metric value is plotted.
